title: metal gear rising: revengeance
text: Do you like doing rad combos like in Devil May Cry? Do you like over-the-top action while super effin' rad music plays in the background? Do you like your games to have a sense of humor? Then by golly gosh darn is this game for you! While MGR:R is not your conventional Metal Gear game, it is still very much worth playing. Developed by Platinum Games (which basically is a label reading, "THIS IS GONNA BE F***ING AWESOME!!!") the game has some fun combat that is as shallow or complex as you want it to be, a bangin' soundtrack, fun costumes, and some of the best damn bosses in any game ever, mainly because of their theme songs (Stranger I Remain AKA Mistral's theme is my favorite)! While this isn't the longest game, being only seven hours long with cutscenes, I always find myself coming back to it just for the crazy, larger-than-life gameplay and characters that have become a staple of the Metal Gear games. As a game I would have to honestly give this game a 7/10, even though I love this game to death and can replay it over and over till the day I die, I cannot give it a higher score because the game put simply is just good not great. I cannot really expain why I say this, but you will definitely understand once you buy and play this. Overall, one of the most fun games I have played and a lowkey favorite of mine in the Metal Gear franchise.

text: Metal Gear Rising is a polarizing game among Metal Gear fans, and most noticeably so for one reason: the gameplay is entirely different from every other game in the series. But that’s the point. Even if it wasn’t a spin-off made by the hack-and-slash Gods over at Platinum Games it would never be a Solid game. It was always designed to be an action game, even when it was originally going to be directed by Kojima’s team. Gameplay demos and trailers of the game before being handed off to Platinum from development hell showed this, while it clearly looked less flashy and slower than the game we got, stealth wasn’t going to be the main focus. Hell, look at the scene where we first see Raiden be the cyborg ninja of MGS4 -- he’s jumping around killing Gekkos in one slice from his HF blade, an enemy which you had been running and stealthing from the entire game so far. Another complaint, and this is one I share myself, is that Revengeance is a slap in the face to the series most tragic character since The Boss, from MGS2 Raiden being a medium for the player and a metaphor for the nature of sequels and thus subverting players expectations of said sequels by ripping Solid Snake from our hands and forcing us to play as a pathetic, baby faced soldier who will never live up to the legend we all saw in MGS1 -- all the way to MG4 where he is lied to by the person he loves and views himself as a failure, but is redeemed throughout the course of the game and given one of the best character arcs in the entire game, being my personal favorite and only surpassed by the Epilogue scene. With Revengeance carrying on from what was a fantastic closure to one of the greatest gaming series of all time appears to be a far greater slap in the face to MGS fans than 5 was. But Platinum, with the help of a little codec retconning that every MGS fan is used to by now, miraculously makes a great game and story for Raiden, letting him be a complete and utter badass just like Snake. I had fun all throughout the game, the gameplay is crisp and sweet in the manner everyone now expects from Platinum, with a nicely sized list of combos and a neat mechanic based around parrying, which if you are terrible at video games like me will be the most difficult yet rewarding thing in the entire game, instead of the dodging seen in Bayonetta. The story also follows many of the points we have all come to love about MGS. Everything from the spectacular political and social critiques, amazing boss battles, and even dealing with the same theme of MGS2, which in itself is a fantastic tribute to all of us who played and loved MGS2. This game is now four years old and I’m a bit late to the party of reviewing it, but if you are for some reason still holding out on buying this game, a Metal Gear fan or not, you will love it. Trust me. Metal Gear Rising is Solid/10

You could miss a lot since there is new codec dialogue even during a boss which if you decided to listen to could break the flow. Combat 8/10 Now here is the tricky part I enjoy the combat of this game but sometimes its a little on the weird side. A lot of things could explode and the hit box lingers, once you learn to parry enemies don't seem as hard anymore. Overall great action game would recommend.

title: metal gear solid v: ground zeroes
text: Looking at all these reviews, it drives me insane to see that the negative reviews are just because of the game's length. Yes, it is indeed very pricey for the amount of product we are given, but it is also so very well executed that it seems like a fair price, in my mind. However, is it worth buying twice? Nah, I picked it up on PS4 because I wanted to give it a spin in terms of curiosity in how it'd play, then afterwards I decided to preorder the Phantom pain. Upon doing so, I was rewarded with a free copy, I played the hell out of it again and got it finished 100% to the end. This is why I'm confused why people think there's only one hour worth of gameplay, no, there really isn't, there is a main mission and there's a good amount of side missions. I'm slightly disappointed that they couldn't at least add a different map that was jungle based, that way you could have a taste of Jungle and Urban doing the day and night. My overall opinion of this game is positive, but I certainly think that they should've given us a little more than they did, a taste of mother base, of buddies, of attatchments, something to overall give us a nudge towards what The Phantom Pain. Yes, we did not get much content for what we paid for, but I feel as though it was a fair enough payment and I'm just fine with having spent the money. Some of the reviews here I think are just people that played the main mission and that's it, no playing the other difficulties or unlocking the other missions, no actually enjoying the game, just going through it and saying 'This is ' and this is what bugs me the most about them. If you're a fan of the series, you will love playing this, but should you pay for this game? At this point? No, wait for 'The Phantom Pain' and just play that. You don't miss much in this game, and even if you do, you can just check informative sites or look at Youtube videos for it. For this content, I'd say my final rating is a 9/10. I love this game, I love this series, I enjoy what they've given us and can't wait for more in the future, the reason why it is only a nine? Because if you read this whole thing then you will know that I did mention I wish they did give us a little more, not a lot more, just at least another small map like this one, maybe a few more weapons, or a buddy, or access to play as some of the troops you recruit from the prisons and as troops for gameplay. Nothing massive like asking for a quarter of the game, no, just something to sweeten the deal.

title: metal gear solid v: ground zeroes
text: MGS V CATCH IT ON SALE! You won't regret it. This game is a stealth game that rewards you for not being seen but gives you the tools and great game engine to load a mag, remove the suppressor, and fight your way in and out. Pros- This game is amazing but only a hour and half long. Once you beat it once you unlock side ops that take place on the same map, with different objectives, troop strength and positions, and every time you play through you unlock new equipment. This is probably to show you the different ways to come at the facility and I have done everything from Guns Blazing to nobody saw me. For example I have snuck in undetected with out being seen or touching a single Marine, saved the hostage, shot may way out of the tunnel, stole a jeep by killing the driver, called for extract, drove to the LZ as the chopper was showing up, and laid suppressive fire till he got low enough to board. These endless on the fly options make even my 10th play through feel drastically different. The control options are amazing. Leaning out from cover to fire, grabbing people up and interrogating them, or choking them out, or cutting their throat, or using them as a shield to fire over their shoulder. All of it a fluid and ridiculously easy to do. While easier to perform actions than MGS4 was there are some moves I miss like rolling on my back and firing up, leaning out to look instead of just to fire, and being able to use the weapon selector switch to swap between single, burst, and full auto. The game is ridiculously well optimize even on the highest setting. Cons- Play this with an official X-Box Remote! The game is picky on what remote you are using and while it does support Keyboard and mouse it is a console port with K+M is an absolute struggle to use. You have to be able to press in the direction of the wall to lean on it, issue is as you spin the camera to look around forward becomes left then back then right then forward again. The problem stems from the fact analog stick was 45 degree angles, keyboards do not. So when you are spinning the camera you tend to jump from cover. Price, $60 is outrageous for this game with such little content, even $20 is kinda steep. I got it on sale for $7 and this game is well worth $7. Put it on your wish list and grab it on sale. TL;DR Pros Ridiculous amount of in game options, from on the fly interacting with the environment, to tools and abilities to use stealth, to being able to easily swap between COD style FPS and Gears of War 3rd person to just Rambo your way in and out. Great Optimization Cons Hour and a Half campaign plus replayability with new objectives and unlocks (All progress transfers to MGS V Phantom Pain) Being a console port Mouse and Keyboard is crude, remote works flawlessly (Use a wired X-Box Remote to circumvent compatibility issues) Price was ridiculous at $60, $20 is far better, when it's on sale its $7 and that's unbeatable....

title: metal gear solid v: ground zeroes
text: MGS Ground Zeroes, worth it for fans, maybe not for newcomers. + Amazing graphics + Fantastic port, 60fps, loads of settings in the options. + Very solid controls, great third person gameplay. + Very sleek and easy to navigate UI. + An astonishing amount of attention to detail. + The base map is designed beautifully for stealth. + 6 very fun side ops, using the same map. + Loads of replayability. + Great teaser for MGS fans for Phantom Pain. - The main mission is roughly 40 minutes long. - Side ops combined, one play through is about 2 or 3 hours long. - The AI is very dumb, they give up pursuit very quickly. - All the guards are telepathic, they instantly alert the entire base, they no longer have to radio in to go on alert like in previous games. - The mouse sensitivity when zoomed in with a sniper rifle far too sensitive. 8/10, if you're a MGS fan, this game is essensial to the series, but get it when it's on sale.

title: metal gear solid v: the phantom pain
text: If I could return this game now, I would. It's terrible on so many levels. The first, and by far the most frustrating, are the controls.  Unholy hell, does this game have absolute garbage controls for the PC.  Zero... and I truly mean ZERO, effort went into developing separate controls for the PC.  Trying to move around, aim or do anything at all is an exercise in controlling frustration for me. I want to run up to a wall, press against it and look around the corner.  So I run at the wall five different times from three different angles and he won't press up against it at all.  In other similar games like Splinter Cell and Deus Ex, this is so easy to accomplish it's like second nature, I don't even realize I'm doing it anymore. I'm 4+ hours in and I still have no clue how to swap weapons.  I did it once by accident through mashing random buttons.  The frakkin industry standard of swapping weapons by using the mouse scroll wheel is simply not present.  Also completely lacking from the game is a comprehensive ability to remap controls.  Don't like what controls the game gives you for the most part?  Tough squash. Second is the story.  I have never played a Hideo Kojima game before, and I never will again.  The story is an incoherent jumble of utterly nonsensical crap.  It's as if a barely literate 15 year old boy went dumpster diving behind a comic book store, and cut and pasted a single story together from 20 different comic books.  I'm 4 hours in, and I have no goddamn clue what is going on, who I'm fighting or why.  When I got to the research and development window and realized that the very first thing the game was going to have me research was a cardboard box, I had to slightly revise my dumpster  diving analogy and add a 6 year old girl into the mix, since my daughter loves to build forts from empty cardboard boxes. Sure, I'm coming in at game five.  I get that, but I came into The Witcher series at game three and had zero problems figuring out the premise of the story and what goal I was supposed to be accomplishing. Another point about story:  I spent the first two hours of the game crawling around on my belly in a hospital. of crawling around while people around me behaved like lobotomized lepers.  I've never been so bored in the opening sequence of a game before in my entire life. My 16 year old son, on the other hand, thinks this game is amazing.  Thank goodness I can share my steam library, so at least someone will get some enjoyment out of this ridiculous exercise in idiocy.

text: There's no question whether MGS5 is worth MSRP or not, but the faults this game has are critical and frustrating. First the good: the gun play and stealth are incredible and unique. Anyone can play the game for a few hours and feel like they're actually Big Boss himself. This is largely due to the controls- it's like they had a team of mathematicians and physicists making sure every single thing Snake did was immaculate. Speaking of breathtaking: the Fox Engine amazes me every single time I boot the game up. It's gorgeous, it's versatile, and it's incredibly stable. The team that made it needs a medal. What of the problems? The story is the main offender. Kojima has always been scatterbrained and unrefined (but that hasn't stopped his rabid fans from trying to rationalize the most asinine of mistakes) but this is just unfinished. You play chapter 1 and you think "How could they mess it up from here?" Then you play chapter 2 and you can almost pinpoint the second when Konami pulled the plug on the funding. In retrospect, even the second environment seems smaller and underdeveloped compared to the first. Next, although the action elements of the gameplay are perfect, the base building sections feel soulless. Mother Base was clearly intended to be less of a plot device and series of menus than it turned out to be. Even the UI feels primitive. Development project trees are somehow confusing in their simplicity. Soldiers are pretty much a spreadsheet management minigame, and the game does expect you to care about them both narratively and mechanically. However, even with these faults, MGS5 isn't a game to skip. You can wait for a sale if you want, but the game is worth it.

title: metal slug 3
text: Before I write this review I want to state that I am a Metal Slug fan. I have played the many ports on the PS2, PS3, Xbox and Xbox360 and so I have a good basis of comparison in writing this review. Metal Slug 3 as it is presented here is advertised as being an 'arcade perfect' port. I think this may be selling itself short: it is better than the arcade. There is zero to negligible slowdown or stuttering throughout the entire game. Most of the nano-second long stuttering I did observe was related to when a Steam Achievement was registered, and some parts in the Final Mission where there were so many items (not bullets) on the screen. There is absolutely none of the 'too-many-bullets' slowdown which is present in the original arcade version and most ports. The gameplay is perfect and you couldn't ask for anything better. (Well, you could, but you wouldn't get it.) Also, thankfully, there is an option to turn on auto-fire from holding the fire button instead of being forced to press it continuously. It's an option I'm glad to have as muscle strain of a long gaming session can distract from the enjoyment of the game. (Extreme purists and people playing for competition don't have to worry as it's only an option that can be turned off completely.) What about visuals? There was a little bit of an uproar among Metal Slug fans when the Xbox360 port of Metal Slug 3 featured a sort of 'upscaling' that made the pixellated art of the game smooth and pseudo-'high-definition'. Especially because there was no way to turn it off. I am happy to say that the version presented here has the full beautiful sprite graphics in all their pixellated glory. They're spectacular, and the resolution really allows you to see the detail the artists put into the game. You can see, for example, the spots on the alien eggs that the clones drop in the Final Mission very clearly. A thing you could not normally make out on a standard arcade cabinet or PS2/Xbox port. There is also an option to turn on a sort of 'smooth' look for the graphics, if you really can't handle the pixels. What about the audio? I am sorry to report there are a few sound effects that sound different from their original arcade and its ports. A person playing the game for the first time would never for a second notice it, but longtime fans will be able to hear the difference right away. It's not too obtrusive: mostly the sound of the 'go' arrow and sounds made by the boss monsters. I can happily say however that the highly-recognizable voice of the announcer, the enemy soldiers, and the player death screams are unchanged. As are the voices of the various POWs. Overall, no one will be upset by this except purists who are used to hearing these sounds hundreds/thousands of times, and even then you can get used to it. I can't help but wonder why the changes. That is, if it has something to do with porting the original sounds or if they could not reuse them for some reason. As you may have seen from the previews, some of the artwork has changed. Most noticeably the portraits on the 'select character' screen. It was a great shock to see that they replaced the classic 'ugly' portraits with new stream-lined ones that aren't dynamic at all. I thought at first that maybe they were trying to move away from the old intentionally 'ugly' art in general, or possibly couldn't use the art due to copyright reasons. But then there is an unlockable gallery that showcases a lot of classic Metal Slug art?! I really don't understand. Thankfully, the art changes begins and ends at the menus and the 'select character' screen. There is an option to play this with online multiplayer, or with two controllers on the same computer. Unfortunately I cannot really report how reliable it is because I was unable to find a partner. Honestly, it doesn't much matter to me. If I finally get a chance to try it and it influences my opinion I will edit this review. edit: I've become aware that the multiplayer is friends-list invite only. This seems a little restrictive, but there you go. As for any possible changes to the game itself, it does feel like they changed a few minor parameters here and there from the original game. It is nothing a newcomer would notice, and overall the game is the same, but during my playthrough for example there were no large number of Heavy Machine Gun items spawning during the fight with the clones in the Final Mission, nor did the piranna give a large amount of bullets on the boat in Mission 1. Again, these are tiny things most players wouldn't notice, but they are there. Fortunately the number of these is very small and was probably done for game balance. As for game options, the game has a standard Easy, Normal, Hard, Very Hard setting. Each game gives the player 20 credits with three lives each, and this cannot be altered in the settings. I always think it's a little strange to not have a menu option to adjust credits from few to infinite, but this does not significantly alter the game. A reasonably skilled person can get through the game in 20 credits just fine. Even if a player is having trouble, there's an option to begin the game from a stage further along, and there should be no difficulty in starting a game on the Final Mission and playing through if you just want to see the ending. Overall, this is possibly the best port of Metal Slug 3 I have ever seen. It has the original pixel-artwork, it gives the player a reasonable amount of credits to win the game, and it performs very well. Its performance is perhaps second only to the PS3 port of Metal Slug 2 with the overclocking set on, but it may even beat that. The only real regret (besides the various changes) is that it does not include the extras 'Fat Island' and 'Storm the Alien Mothership' mini-games that were present only in the Xbox and JPS2 ports of Metal Slug 3, but that may have been too much to hope for. I recommend buying this game. I hope this release brings a success that convinces them to eventually bring all Metal Slug games to Steam.

title: metro 2033 redux
text: Metro 2033 Redux  is a remastered FPS based on a popular novel of the same name. You play a young Russian named Artyum during the year 2033 who lives among others in an underground bunker due to the world around you being eradicated by nuclear warfare. Now there's nothing but destroyed buildings and mutants walking among the lands. Oh and Nazis and Commies , they're there too! This is a fantastic game , that has a few hiccups that may or may not have to do with the engine upgrade however the storyline and the characters are so interesting and whacky that there's a lot here to be into. The gameplay is pretty great too. For such a small team to create this game , it's impressive and I can see why it has the following now it has. Pros: -Story is really great. It's not the most "wowing" story of all time but it's interesting. -The way things look , the broken buildings , the bunkers and stations filled with people talking to each other and military , the mutants, the way some of the particles look in the dark look really fantastic. Sometimes you'll find yourself stopping to hear full conversations with some of the npcs around the bunkers. Some fascinating stuff that really fleshes out the world, I really wish more games would do this. -Gameplay kinda feels like an early FPS and it's fun to stealth around a map and take someone out as well. -AI is very smart in some spots of the game. -The choice of Survival or Spartan mode before playing. I went Survival just to get the full experience. -The music is really great too. Lots of acoustic and some piano. Some really spooky stuff at times and a lot of it makes the game. -A lot of your comrades are real characters and you'll enjoy their parts of the story. One of them is hilarious. Bit*ches! -Some fun secrets to find if you can get off the beaten path. Cons: -At some point of the game you obtain Night Vision. And the game does not explain to you how to get it to work out side of saying "hit the N Key". You get a charger early in the game , like super early. That they ALSO do not explain how to use, this powers up your Night Vision and your Flashlight. Just gotta hold F and click.... -The game also does not explain how to use the Later in the game. You have to hold R and click to pump it... Very important. -Since I Played on survival , the ammo etc is more scarse. But for some reason around Chapter 5-6 there's like no ammo , anywhere. Period. You run out , you're screwed. The last chapter or so was a nightmare for me because all I had was my and no ammo for any of the guns. I even picked up a new gun and it had like 3 ammo. Was very upset by this. -Keys are like easy to find for the first 3 chapters then it just becomes a mess. You'll end up finding vaults before you find keys...Wish they made this slightly easier, maybe highlight keys more. Things get more dicey when there's 2 keys in a level.. -Wiping your Gas Mask feels useless. Just smears sh*it all across the screen , unless it's blood...that goes away. Mixed: *Nitpicking* -Just wish there were more gun types , more playstales. I feel like every gun even when you fully customize them is super limited and the reloads take forever. It could be because I played on Survival though. -Some graphical glitches occur throughout the game, I actually noticed this happens in the trailer for Redux too. It's not enough to bother you but they exist. Especially when characters sweat. Anyways play this game. The libarians are scary as fu*ck. Enjoy. Gonna start Last Light now.
